episodes.title: Who Sampled?:  Charles Manson Edition [True Crime Special #1]
episodes.description:
Charles Manson was an American criminal and cult leader whose name became synonymous with manipulation, violence, and one of the most infamous murder cases in modern history. Born on November 12, 1934, in Cincinnati, Ohio, Manson had a troubled childhood marked by neglect, crime, and repeated stints in reform schools and prisons. He spent much of his early life institutionalized, where he developed a deep resentment toward authority and society.

In the late 1960s, after his release from prison, Manson moved to California and began attracting followers, mostly young people searching for purpose during the countercultural era. This group became known as the “Manson Family.” Living primarily at the Spahn Ranch near Los Angeles, Manson exerted psychological control over his followers, using a mix of charisma, pseudo-philosophy, and manipulation. He preached an apocalyptic vision he called “Helter Skelter,” which he interpreted from songs by The Beatles, believing a race war was imminent.

In August 1969, Manson directed members of his group to carry out a series of brutal murders. The most notorious of these took place at the home of actress Sharon Tate, who was eight months pregnant at the time. Tate and four others were killed in a horrific attack. The following night, another couple, Leno and Rosemary LaBianca, were also murdered. Although Manson did not personally commit the killings, he orchestrated them, making him legally responsible.

Manson and several of his followers were arrested later that year and put on trial in 1970. The trial attracted massive media attention due to the shocking nature of the crimes and the eerie devotion of his followers, who often behaved erratically in court. In 1971, Manson was convicted of first-degree murder and conspiracy to commit murder. He was initially sentenced to death, but the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment after California temporarily abolished the death penalty.

Manson spent the remainder of his life in prison, becoming a symbol of evil and psychological manipulation. He died on November 19, 2017, at the age of 83. His story continues to fascinate and disturb people, serving as a grim reminder of how influence and ideology can be twisted into something deadly.

This video features 30 examples of songs that sampled mostly dialogue from various interviews he gave throughout his time in prison. I hope you enjoy it.
